content:
Cortex Trade is the keyword for trading robots sold from eacortex.com, which the site brands as Cortex AI. The homepage prices its Mobile and PC robots in South African rand, names no legal entity and gives no regulator. Its refund wording is much narrower than the headline guarantee.

The reference site for this review is eacortex.com. The review sets out what the site says and what we could not check.

Here is what the reference site states and what it leaves out.

CategoryWhat the site says

PricesMobile Robot R1,000 one-off; PC Robot R1,500 one-off. 7-day trial terms not explained
Minimum depositNot stated by the site

Refunds24 hours, only for a verified technical fault that stops the robot working
MarketsForex, stocks, crypto and commodities, including XAUUSD, USDJPY and EURUSD
SupportTelegram, email and WhatsApp; stated hours 08:00 to 22:00 SAST
Operator and regulatorNot stated. The 'lifetime licence' is a software licence

Items come from the platform's own site. We have not tested the platform.

Is Cortex Trade Legit? What the Claims Show

Performance and the success rate

The site cites a 75% success rate defined only as consistent profitable trades. It gives no time period, sample size or method, and the R15K daily average has no source. The live dashboard may be illustrative, and the site does not say whether it shows real account data.

Refunds and withdrawals

The headline reads as a 24-hour refund guarantee, but the policy excludes incorrect installation, unsupported devices, market changes and any change of mind after activation. The FAQ asks about withdrawing profits, but no answer is given.

Testimonials

Screenshots are labelled as verified and all rated 5.0. They show large percentage gains and single-day results, but no account verification, time frames or losing trades. Some reviewers appear to share a name.

Costs and Minimum Deposit

The site does not state a minimum deposit or a full fee schedule. Ask for both in writing before any commitment.

Our standard minimum deposit for this review is 250 in the reader's local currency: AUD 250 in Australia, GBP 250 in the UK and EUR 250 in the EU. The site's own figures, if any, are shown above, so confirm the exact amount in the terms before you deposit.

Who Is Behind Cortex Trade

The site names the Cortex AI brand with a 2026 copyright, but no legal entity, company number or address. It links purchases to whop.com and to algoproedge.com, and the site does not explain how these businesses relate.

Cortex AI review and scam check

The site uses the Cortex AI brand, while our keyword is Cortex Trade. Confirm you are reviewing the same product, and search the brand name together with 'complaints' and 'refund' before paying.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Find the legal company behind Cortex Trade and check it against the regulator's register in your country.
  • Ask for a written fee schedule, minimum deposit and withdrawal terms before you fund an account.
  • Ask for dated, verifiable performance records rather than testimonials or a single rating.
  • Start with the smallest amount you can afford to lose, and use any demo account first.

Risks to Keep in Mind

The risk disclaimer warns that trading can lose money, but it sits beside guaranteed-sounding phrasing and 24/7 claims. A lifetime software licence does not protect the trading results of the robot itself.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Cortex Trade legit?

The site names no operator, licence or address, and its success and profit figures have no stated method. Check the company details and the refund conditions before you buy.

How much does Cortex Trade cost?

The robots are priced at R1,000 (Mobile) and R1,500 (PC), one-off. The site gives no broker, VPS or extension costs.

Is there a Cortex Trade minimum deposit?

The site does not state a minimum deposit. The deposit you need depends on your broker. Our standard minimum deposit for this review is 250 in the reader's local currency: AUD 250 in Australia, GBP 250 in the UK and EUR 250 in the EU.

Does Cortex Trade offer a refund?

There is a 24-hour refund window, but only for a verified technical fault. Read the exclusions before you buy.

Can a trading robot remove the risk of losing money?

No. The site's own disclaimer says trading can lose money and results are not guaranteed.

Our Verdict on Cortex Trade

Cortex Trade sells software at fixed rand prices, but its performance claims have no method, its refund is narrow, and the operator is not named. Check these points before any purchase. Our rating reflects these gaps. We will revisit it once the operator and its claims can be confirmed.
